name: State of AI 2026: NYC Launch Event
why: Fireside conversations as Air Street launches the 2026 State of AI Report, with author Nathan Benaich and Ramp's lead economist Ara Kharazian.

name: Daytona AI Builders: NYC
why: Short talks on forkable sandboxes for long-running agents, multi-agent systems on Bedrock AgentCore, and world models for production agents, with networking and pizza after.

name: NousCon 2026
why: Exhibits and networking from 6 PM with the Nous Research team around the future of Hermes Agent and open intelligence, followed by a party until midnight.

name: Gemini 4 Argon NYC Hackathon
why: One-day hackathon with Google DeepMind on Gemini 4 Argon, with $20,000 in cash prizes across tracks spanning advanced reasoning, visual coding, robotics, and world models; teams up to four.

name: Winter Village at Bryant Park — Ice Skating Opens
why: Outdoor ice skating rink opens for the season at Bryant Park's Winter Village, running through February 28.

name: Wollman Rink — Ice Skating Opens
why: Classic Central Park outdoor ice skating rink reopens for the season, running through March 16.

name: Lefrak Center at Lakeside — Ice Skating Opens
venue: Lefrak Center at Lakeside, Prospect Park
why: Prospect Park's outdoor ice skating rink at Lakeside opens for the 2026–27 season.

name: Gottesman Rink at the Davis Center — Ice Skating Opens
why: The Gottesman Rink at the Davis Center in Central Park opens for the season on November 1, running through March 7.

name: Roebling Rink at Brooklyn Bridge Park — Ice Skating Opens
why: Outdoor ice skating rink at Brooklyn Bridge Park opens November 14, running through January 31.

name: An Evening with the New York Times Op-Docs 2026, Part 1
why: Screening of four acclaimed New York Times Op-Docs short documentaries, followed by a discussion with the filmmakers and Op-Docs team.

name: Junk Journal Hang and Zine Trade
why: Drop-in session to create junk journals and trade zines at Purgatory in Bushwick; supplies provided, bring your own to share.

name: Letters + Sodas Reading Series
why: Lana Schwartz (The New Yorker, McSweeney's) hosts a night of standup, humor pieces, fiction, and essay readings in LIC.

name: The Vinyl Word: The Smiths vs. The Cure
why: Back-to-back album listening party pitting The Smiths' The Queen is Dead against The Cure's Disintegration, with the crowd voting on the winner.

name: Southern Oracles
why: The Black Air Poets fuse jazz, hip hop, poetry, dance, and more in a multidisciplinary concert exploring the music, history, and culture of the South.

name: Ditmas Lit Reading Series
why: Fiction writers, storytellers, poets, and essayists — Andrew Colarusso, Margaret Kogan, Maxim Matusevich, and Kailee Pederson — share new work at the Ditmas Lit series.

name: Newsreel: Midterm Mania Panel + Party
why: Phone-free midterm election panel five days before Election Day, with NYC Council Member Chi Ossé, Vox's Astead Herndon, and Batya Ungar-Sargon, followed by a DJ party.

name: Carnegie Science Spooky Social
why: Astronomer Dr. Scott Sheppard explores hidden planets, 'planet-killer' asteroids, and mysteries of our solar system in a spooky Halloween-themed science evening with trivia, prizes, and optional costume contest.

name: Final Reading: Center for Fiction / Susan Kamil 2026 Emerging Writer Fellows
why: Nine 2026 Emerging Writer Fellows wrap up their cohort year by reading from their published writing and works in progress.

name: The Sixth Annual Francon
why: Annual tribute to NYC writer and humorist Fran Lebowitz where fans swap books, smoke candy cigarettes, and drink themed cocktails at the Holiday Cocktail Lounge.

name: Grand Central Terminal Tour
why: Guided architectural tour of Grand Central Terminal with MAS docents; multiple dates and times available.

name: From Fur & Flowers to Fashion: West 20s Tour
why: Walking tour with Matt Postal exploring the West 20s neighborhood's history from fur traders and flower markets to its transformation into a fashion district.

name: Art Deco Murray Hill/Gramercy Tour
why: Walking tour with Anthony W. Robins through the Art Deco architecture of Murray Hill and Gramercy neighborhoods.

name: Aaron Gilbert: Alex Katz Chair in Painting Artist Talk
venue: Frederick P. Rose Auditorium, Cooper Union
why: Painter Aaron Gilbert, whose work depicts intimate everyday scenes from his Brooklyn microcosm against fluorescent institutional backdrops, gives an artist talk at Cooper Union.

name: Public Art Fund Talk: Genesis Belanger
source: Public Art Fund / The Cooper Union
why: Genesis Belanger and Public Art Fund Senior Curator Melanie Kress discuss Belanger's first major public exhibition in NYC, three site-responsive sculptural installations at City Hall Park exploring value, justice, and artifice.

name: New York Architecture & Design Publishing Today
venue: Arthur A. Houghton Jr. Gallery, Cooper Union
source: The Cooper Union School of Architecture
why: Roundtable with editors and publishers of Log/Any, A83, Architectural Design, Table, Untapped, Head Hi, and New York Review of Architecture on what it means to publish architecture discourse today.

name: Christine Chang: Dialogue as Method — Objects, Thresholds & Off-Modern Ruins
why: Christine Chang of Neri&Hu traces three projects that weave fictional narratives, East Asian spatial frameworks, and adaptive reuse through a lecture on design knowledge built from material failures and in-situ confrontations.

name: Goodbye, Dragon Inn
why: Tsai Ming-liang's astonishingly beautiful film set entirely in one decaying movie theater, a rueful backwards glance at the disappearing filmgoing culture of his youth — one of the seminal films of the 21st century.

name: Sneak Preview: The Meltdown (El deshielo) with Director Manuela Martelli
why: Chile's 2027 Oscar submission for Best International Feature screens with director Manuela Martelli in person; set in 1992 during Chile's post-Pinochet 'economic miracle,' following a nine-year-old girl at an Andean ski resort.

name: Kubrick Retrospective — Opens with The Shining
why: Complete film retrospective of Stanley Kubrick presented by Criterion, running Nov 1–Dec 26; opens with the U.S. theatrical premiere of The Shining's International Release cut, followed by the American version, with Steadicam inventor Garrett Brown and archivist Michael Chaiken in person.

name: How to Use Agents and Not Have Them Kill You (AI Workshop)
venue: MoMI LAB, Museum of the Moving Image
why: One-hour workshop explaining what AI agents actually are and how they differ from other AI, using examples from film, gaming, and media.

name: Fall Yoga with The Yoga Room at MoMI
source: Museum of the Moving Image / The Yoga Room
why: Free one-hour yoga class indoors at the Museum most Sundays Nov 8–Dec 27, doors open at 11 AM.

name: First Responders Appreciation Night at MCNY
venue: Museum of the City of New York
source: Museum of the City of New York
via: Museum of the City of New York
why: Free late-night Wednesday at MCNY celebrating NYC first responders — full gallery access, guided tour, and an ice cream giveaway for the first 100 responders who show credentials; cash bar.

name: The Occupied City: Revolutionary New York, 1763–1790
venue: Museum of the City of New York
source: Museum of the City of New York
via: Museum of the City of New York
why: Immersive third-floor exhibition tracing NYC's transformation from colonial port to newly independent city through the Revolutionary era (1763–1790), exploring occupation, resistance, and the city's founding contradictions.

name: Exclusive Tour Inside the Woolworth Building: NYC's Cathedral of Commerce
why: Guided behind-the-scenes tour of the Woolworth Building's ornate lobby, mosaic ceilings, and historic details; runs on multiple dates through December.

name: After-Hours Pastel Painting Workshop @ AKC Museum of the Dog
why: After-hours pastel painting workshop inside the AKC Museum of the Dog, surrounded by historic canine art.

name: Brooklyn Heights at Twilight: The Weird, Wonderful, and In-Between
why: Twilight walking tour through Brooklyn Heights exploring its eccentric architectural history, hidden passages, and offbeat landmarks.

name: Secrets of the East River: NYC's Hidden Infrastructure by Ferry
why: Ferry tour revealing the hidden infrastructure lining the East River — power plants, sewage treatment, prison islands, and more — with an expert guide.

name: Underground Manhattan: Exploring the History of the NYC Subway System
why: Guided exploration of the NYC subway system's hidden history, abandoned stations, and architectural gems with an expert guide.

name: Exclusive Trip Inside the Loew's Valencia: NYC's First 'Wonder Theatre'
why: Behind-the-scenes tour of the Loew's Valencia, one of the five 'Wonder Theatres' built in the late 1920s — an atmospheric movie palace with an ornate Spanish baroque interior.

name: Exploring the Ghosts of New York City's Elevated Railroads
why: Walking tour tracing the vanished elevated train lines — the Second and Third Avenue Els — through the ghost infrastructure that still haunts city blocks.

name: After-Hours Conservation Lab Tour @ The New-York Historical Society
why: After-hours guided tour of the New-York Historical Society's conservation lab, where staff restore and preserve rare artifacts, books, and artworks from the collection.

name: The Secret World of Flowers: Behind-the-Scenes NYC Floral District Tour
why: Early-morning behind-the-scenes tour of the NYC Floral District on West 28th Street, once the center of the American cut-flower trade.

name: The Secret Eats of Arthur Avenue Food Crawl: The Bronx's Little Italy
why: Guided food crawl through Arthur Avenue in the Bronx, NYC's authentic Little Italy, sampling from Italian bakeries, butchers, cheese shops, and restaurants.

name: Tracing the Battle of Brooklyn: A Revolutionary War Battlefield Walk
why: Walking tour retracing the 1776 Battle of Brooklyn — the largest battle of the American Revolution — through Prospect Park and across the neighborhoods where it unfolded.

name: The Garbage That Built New York: A Walk Through NYC's Trash & Rat History
why: Walking tour through the history of NYC's waste management — from landfill islands to the Great Sanitation Strike — exploring how trash shaped the city's geography and politics.

name: Behind the Scenes @ New York Society Library: NYC's Oldest Library
why: Behind-the-scenes tour of the New York Society Library, founded in 1754 and the oldest library in New York City, exploring its rare collections and history.

name: Alexander Hamilton's New York: Tracing the American Founding Father's Steps
why: Walking tour through Alexander Hamilton's New York — from his home near Wall Street to the sites of his duels, business dealings, and political battles.

name: Exploring the Seaside Village of City Island
why: Guided exploration of City Island in the Bronx, a surprisingly New England–feeling maritime village of shipyards, seafood shacks, and Victorian cottages.

name: Behind-the-Scenes @ Lincoln Center: Extended Tour Inside Iconic Halls
venue: Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts
why: Extended behind-the-scenes tour of Lincoln Center's concert halls, backstage areas, and iconic spaces — the Metropolitan Opera, David Geffen Hall, and more.

name: Gargoyles of Greenwich Village: Exploring the Neighborhood's Stone Bestiary
why: Walking tour through Greenwich Village spotting the gargoyles, grotesques, and decorative stone animals that guard its historic buildings — a brand new NYAC debut event.

name: Exclusive Caviar 101 & Hands-On Tasting @ Urbani Truffle Lab NYC
why: Tasting class sampling multiple varieties of caviar with expert guidance on grading, pairing, and the history of caviar production at the Urbani Truffle Lab.

name: Live from the NY2044 Newsdesk: Hope and Historias
venue: Flamboyán Theater at The Clemente Center
why: Immersive live launch of Issue 4 of New York 2044, a speculative newspaper imagining the city's future, featuring live performance with video projections, a soundscape by Rabbistravinski, and reports from three contributors — followed by discussion moderated by UO founding editor Cassim Shepard.

name: Pumpkitecture! Architectural Pumpkin Carving Competition
source: AIA New York / Center for Architecture
why: Annual architectural pumpkin carving competition at the Center for Architecture — this year's theme is interiors; compete as a firm or spectate.

name: Reimagining the Li Lu Law Library at Columbia Law School
source: AIA New York / Center for Architecture
why: Architecture talk presenting the recent renovation and reimagining of the Li Lu Law Library at Columbia Law School — design process, challenges, and outcomes.

name: The Pulse Nightclub Memorial: Designing for Remembrance and Healing
source: AIA New York / Center for Architecture
why: The City of Orlando presents the design process for the Pulse Nightclub Memorial, exploring how architects approach dignified remembrance of a mass tragedy site.

name: Building of the Day: Vagelos Innovation Laboratories
why: Archtober building tour of the Vagelos Innovation Laboratories, a Columbia University research facility by Skidmore, Owings & Merrill designed for collaborative science.

name: Archtober x Data Vandals: Rats in the City Costume Competition
why: Halloween costume competition celebrating NYC rats, hosted by Archtober and Data Vandals, with prizes for the best rat-inspired costumes and data-driven presentations on the city's rodent infrastructure.

name: Center for Architecture Fall Exhibitions
why: Three exhibitions currently on view: 'Humanist Modernity: Maciej and Stanisława Nowicki' (through Mar 27), 'Dark Matter U: Justice, Pedagogy, Design' (through Mar 27), and 'Why Design?' (through Jan 2).

name: NYPL Horror Film Series: Slashers
why: Free horror film screening at the main NYPL branch — slasher classics for Halloween week.

name: The Addams Family (1991) 35th Anniversary Screening
why: 35th anniversary free screening of Barry Sonnenfeld's The Addams Family (1991) at the main NYPL branch.

name: Lesia Ukrainka: Ukraine's Forgotten Playwright
why: Discussion of Ukrainian playwright and poet Lesia Ukrainka's life and legacy, presented at NYPL with a hybrid attendance option.

name: Ghostbusters (1984) Free Screening
venue: Library for the Performing Arts at Lincoln Center
why: Halloween free screening of Ghostbusters (1984) at the Library for the Performing Arts.

name: Library After Hours: Friday the 13th
why: After-hours Halloween-themed evening event inside the Schwarzman Building, open after regular hours for a special ticketed program.

name: NYPL Fall Exhibitions: Winnie-the-Pooh, Declaring America, Forging Ahead, Unleashed
why: Four concurrent exhibitions on view at the main branch: Winnie-the-Pooh and the Origins of the Hundred Acre Wood, Declaring America, Forging Ahead, and Unleashed.

name: From Field to Form: Ocean Flora
why: Panel exploring the use of marine biomaterials — sargassum, seagrass, and kelp — in architecture and construction, with panelists Iván García Kerdan, Shanjana Mahmud, and Tobias Øhrstrøm, moderated by Mae-ling Lokko.

name: America's 250th Anniversary Walking Tour of Fort Greene Park
venue: Fort Greene Park (DeKalb Ave/Washington Park entrance)
why: Walking tour tracing Fort Greene Park's role in the Revolutionary War — the Battle of Brooklyn, the Prison Ship Martyrs, and the founding of the park — led by historians Natasha Fearon and Alexandra Stevens as part of Brooklyn 250.

name: Black History & Culture Tour of Fort Greene Park
venue: Fort Greene Park (DeKalb Ave/Washington Park entrance)
why: Guided tour covering The Heart of Black Fort Greene and Fort Greene Black History Makers and Cultural Giants — stops spanning the 1800s to today, led by historian Suzanne Spellen; developed with BlackSpace, MoCADA, and Weeksville Heritage Center.

name: Chelsea Piers Fitness Run Club at Fort Greene Park
source: Fort Greene Park Conservancy / Chelsea Piers Fitness
why: Free 3–5 mile group run starting at the Fort Greene Park monument, led by Coach Skye Massey; runs Tuesdays through November 3.

name: Fort Greene Park Artisans Bazaar
why: Weekly Saturday open-air market along DeKalb Ave with 30+ local designers, artisans, and makers — upcycled fashion, jewelry, apothecary, candles, and food.

name: In the Room: David Hume Kennerly — 60 Years on the Front Lines of History
venue: The Cooper Union Great Hall, 7 East 7th Street
why: Pulitzer Prize-winning photojournalist David Hume Kennerly discusses 60 years of iconic images — from the RFK assassination to Vietnam, every U.S. president, and the rise of fascist policing — with ABC News Presidential Historian Mark K. Updegrove, on the occasion of his Rizzoli career retrospective.

name: Haunted History: The Age of the Witch Hunts
why: In-person class exploring the history of European and American witch trial panics — the social, religious, and political forces that drove mass accusations and executions.

name: Red Hook Defiant: Revolutionary War Walking Tour
venue: Red Hook Interim Library, 362 Van Brunt Street
why: A new walking tour from Brainery teacher and guide Daniel Pecoraro tracing Red Hook's role in the Battle of Brooklyn — harbor and land defenses, the contested location of Fort Defiance, and sites of Revolutionary War memorial.

name: So Who Was Van Brunt Anyway? Naming Red Hook Walking Tour
venue: Red Hook Interim Library, 362 Van Brunt Street
why: New walking tour by Daniel Pecoraro tracing the history behind Red Hook's street and park names — Van Brunt, Coffey, Ferris — weaving the neighborhood's broader history into how NYC streets get named and co-named.

name: Queens Tech+Innovation Challenge Kickoff Night
why: Kickoff event for the Queens Tech+Innovation Challenge with Queens Borough President Donovan Richards — civic tech competition launching across the borough.

name: AI DevCon 2026
why: AI developer conference at Industry City with speakers including Nick Carmont (Applied AI, Anthropic), Steve Yegge (creator, Gas Town), Geoffrey Huntley, and Baruch Sadogursky — focused on building and deploying AI agents.

name: Six Math Essentials with Terence Tao
why: Free public talk by Fields Medal–winning mathematician Terence Tao at Pioneer Works — one of the most celebrated living mathematicians presenting accessible mathematical ideas at Brooklyn's premier science and arts venue.
